chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Eating quince is strengthening for the weak heart, it sweetens the stomach, sharpens the intellect/heart, and emboldens the timid.'
ai.seo_question: What are the health and spiritual benefits of eating quince according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this narration chains back to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) quoting Imam Ali (AS), reflecting the Shia tradition of integrating physical health with spiritual fortitude. The quince (safarjal) is presented not merely as a dietary item but as a therapeutic agent that strengthens the heart, purifies the stomach, sharpens the mind (fawad), and instills courage in the timid, illustrating the holistic view of well-being in prophetic medicine.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eating the Quince is strengthening for the weak heart and aromatises the stomach, and purifies the heart, and emboldens the timid’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Qasim ibn Yahya from his grandfather al-Hassan ibn Rashid who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin has said,
’Eating quince strengthens the weak heart, cleanses the stomach, purifies the mind and emboldens the coward/”
